reader.requirement: A sequential file's record order must be the order in which WRITEs created it (OPEN OUTPUT starts the order over), a REWRITE in I-O mode must not move a record, and the order changes only by records appended at the end in EXTEND mode, for fixed and RECORD VARYING records alike; the witness covers fixed records with one REWRITE and one EXTEND.

edition-consulted.switches: SharingFacilityInEffect: at 85 a second connector's OPEN EXTEND or OUTPUT of the open file is 41, so no other writer can interleave with or truncate the order; from 2002 Table 19 decides
OtherConnectorsMayShare (FileSharingFacility): flush per WRITE and medium-counted ordinal only from 2002
the EXTEND arm's ordinal seeding asks FileLockPosture.AdmitsAnotherWriter(HostShare) (AllOther at 85); OUTPUT Create and EXTEND Append are the same at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep of DialectBehavior, Edition, SharingFacilityInEffect, HostShare in SequentialConnector.cs and FileRegistry.cs; the ordering itself (append-only writer, OUTPUT truncation, in-place REWRITE) is edition-independent
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a sibling connector cannot open the file to append beside the owner (41); from 2002 a Table 19 admitted sibling may. The order produced by one connector's WRITE, REWRITE and EXTEND is the same.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf21_02 covers fixed records, one REWRITE, one EXTEND; not exercised are OPEN OUTPUT over an existing file restarting the order, RECORD VARYING records of differing lengths, a refused sibling EXTEND, two successive EXTENDs, and a REVERSED read of the established order

reader.notes: The order comes from an append-only writer (OUTPUT Create, EXTEND Append) and an in-place REWRITE through the reader's stream; at 85 the 41 refusal in SharedOpenAttempt keeps any second connector from appending or truncating while the file is open, so the deleted 85 sibling-release machinery has no case left to serve. Same comment drift as the GR7 record (the EnsureReaderCoherent summary and the OpenCore OUTPUT arm describe an admitted 85 sibling OPEN OUTPUT).

refuter.evidence: r3-001 at --std 85: F1 OPEN OUTPUT two 8-char records, CLOSE; F2 (second SELECT, same path, RECORD VARYING 1-8 DEPENDING ON) OPEN OUTPUT over the existing file writes 'AAA'(3), 'BBBBBBB'(7); F1 OPEN EXTEND 'C'(1); F2 OPEN EXTEND 'DDDDD'(5); then F1 OPEN INPUT, one READ, and mid-read sibling OPEN EXTEND F2 and OPEN OUTPUT F2. Printed 'R1 03 [AAA] / SIBLING EXTEND MID-READ 41 / SIBLING OUTPUT MID-READ 41 / R 01 07 [BBBBBBB] / R 02 01 [C] / R 03 05 [DDDDD]': OPEN OUTPUT through another connector restarts the successor relationship (the OLD1OLD1 records are gone), two successive EXTENDs through different connectors append in execution order at their own lengths (GR13), and the refused sibling OPENs leave the reader's position and the order unaffected. Class c refusals as for GR7 (r2, r2b, r2c COBOL0900). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR12  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR12'; 'OK  §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR13  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR13'; 'OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.4a'. The NoteRelease() removal in OpenCore's OUTPUT arm matters to GR12 only through a reader open beside the truncating OUTPUT, which at 85 answers 41 (r3-001) and from 2002 Table 19 refuses; a later OPEN re-seeds the reader's _coherentAt (SequentialConnector.cs lines 398 and 2426), so a reader re-opened after the truncation sees the new order. Not re-probed on a rebuilt tree.
